questions.question: The price of 24 movie tickets is ₹768. How much (in ₹) will 32 movie tickets cost? [Assume that all tickets here are equally priced]
questions.solution:

The price of 24 movie tickets is ₹768.

Cost per ticket = Total Cost / Number of Tickets

Total cost for 32 tickets = Cost per ticket x Number of Tickets

**Calculation:**

Cost per ticket = ₹768 / 24

⇒ Cost per ticket = ₹32

Total cost for 32 tickets = ₹32 x 32

⇒ Total cost for 32 tickets = ₹1024

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper promises to sell his goods at cost price. However, he uses a weight that actually weighs 49% less than what is written on it. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:

Weight used = 49% less than actual

Actual weight = 100%

Used weight = 100% - 49% = 51%

**Formula used:**

Profit% = frac{{Extra gain}}{{Cost Price}} × 100

Cost price of 51g = ₹51

Selling price = ₹100

⇒ Profit = 100 - 51 = ₹49

⇒ Profit% = (49)/(51) × 100

questions.question: In which of the following years was the 'Quit India Movement' launched?

__
 
• The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on **8 August 1942**, during World War II, demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• Gandhi delivered the iconic "Do or Die" speech at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• The movement is also known as the **August Kranti** or August Movement.
 
• The British responded with mass arrests and repression, detaining many leaders of the Indian National Congress without trial.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World War II Context**

 
 
• The Quit India Movement occurred during the turbulent times of World War II, when British resources were stretched thin.
 
• India's contribution to the British war effort was significant, which led to increasing demands for self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Arrest of Leaders**
 
 
• Following the launch of the movement, the British arrested nearly all leaders of the Indian National Congress, including Gandhi, Nehru, and Patel.
 
• This led to a leaderless movement, which saw widespread but uncoordinated protests across the country.
 
 
 
• **Public Response**
 
 
• Despite the lack of central leadership, the movement saw massive public participation, including strikes, protests, and acts of civil disobedience.
 
• The British government responded with severe repression, including police violence, mass detentions, and press censorship.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Independence**
 
 
• Though the Quit India Movement was ultimately suppressed, it significantly intensified the Indian struggle for independence.
 
• It demonstrated the Indian population's unified demand for freedom, which played a crucial role in the eventual British decision to leave India in 1947.

questions.question: In the case of reptiles, their heart is not properly divided in to four chambers i.e., it consists of two auricles and an incompletely divided ventricle. Which of the following is an example of a reptile having a four-chambered heart?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Crocodiles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Crocodiles are unique among reptiles for having a fully divided four-chambered heart, similar to that of birds and mammals.
 
• This four-chambered heart includes two atria and two ventricles, ensuring complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood.
 
• The structure allows crocodiles to maintain a high metabolic rate, which is beneficial for their predatory lifestyle.
 
• The presence of a four-chambered heart in crocodiles is an evolutionary adaptation that supports their amphibious mode of life, allowing efficient respiration both in water and on land.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reptilian Heart Structure:**

 
 
• Most reptiles typically have a three-chambered heart consisting of two atria and one ventricle, with some degree of ventricular septation.
 
• This partial separation allows for the mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, which is sufficient for their metabolic needs.
 
 
 
• **Double Circulation:**
 
 
• Double circulation refers to the separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood within the heart, which is a feature seen in crocodiles and is characteristic of a four-chambered heart.
 
• This system allows for more efficient oxygen delivery to the body tissues.
 
 
 
• **Evolutionary Significance:**
 
 
• The fully divided heart in crocodiles is considered an advanced evolutionary trait, providing a physiological advantage in terms of metabolic efficiency and thermoregulation.
 
• This adaptation is also seen in birds, which share a common ancestor with crocodiles.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Mammals and Birds:**
 
 
• Both mammals and birds possess a four-chambered heart, which evolved independently in these groups.
 
• The presence of a four-chambered heart in crocodiles is a case of convergent evolution, where similar traits evolve independently in different lineages.

questions.question: Which Articles of the Constitution of India provide for a parliamentary form of government at the Centre?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 74 and 75**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 74 of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President.
 
• Article 75 specifies that the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President, and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• These articles collectively establish the framework for the parliamentary system of government in India, where the executive authority is derived from and accountable to the legislature.
 
• The Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, the lower house of Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parliamentary System of Government:**

 
 
• In a parliamentary system, the executive branch derives its legitimacy from the legislature and is accountable to it.
 
• The head of state is different from the head of government.
 
 
 
• **Collective Responsibility:**
 
 
• The principle that the executive (Council of Ministers) is collectively responsible to the legislature (Lok Sabha).
 
• If the Lok Sabha passes a vote of no-confidence, the entire Council of Ministers must resign.
 
 
 
• **President's Role:**
 
 
• The President of India acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• This ensures that the real executive power is vested in the elected representatives of the people.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister's Role:**
 
 
• The Prime Minister is the head of the government and leads the executive branch.
 
• Plays a critical role in formulating and executing policies, and in maintaining the support of the majority in the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Article ________ A supplements the 11th fundamental duty of the Indian Constitution?

• The concept of fundamental duties is inspired by the Constitution of Russia (erstwhile Soviet Union).
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law but are considered essential for citizens.
 
 
 
• **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002:**
 
 
• This amendment made three significant changes: introducing Article 21A, adding the 11th fundamental duty, and modifying Article 45.
 
• Article 21A makes education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• Article 45 was revised to focus on early childhood care and education for children below the age of six years.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education Act, 2009:**

questions.question: A person having stunted growth and discoloured hair is most probably suffering from ________________.

• Other symptoms of protein deficiency may include muscle wasting, edema, and an enlarged abdomen.
 
• A diet rich in legumes, nuts, dairy products, meat, and fish can help prevent protein deficiency.

• A severe form of malnutrition caused by an inadequate intake of protein.

• Symptoms include edema, irritability, ulcerating dermatoses, and an enlarged liver.
 
 
 
• **Marasmus**:
 
 
• Another form of severe malnutrition caused by an overall lack of calories and protein.
 
• Characterized by severe wasting of body fat and muscle, leading to a "skin and bones" appearance.
 
• Common among children in regions with food scarcity.
 
 
 
• **Essential Amino Acids**:
 
 
• Amino acids that the body cannot synthesize on its own and must be obtained from the diet.
